title: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938): Risks and Mitigations
content_md: On November 17, 2026, a memory corruption vulnerability in the OpenJDK HotSpot runtime was publicly disclosed and assigned CVE-2026-114938. The security firm Calif, which discovered the vulnerability, dubbed it "Java4Shell." The disclosure was accompanied by coordinated advisories from Oracle, the OpenJDK project, Red Hat (RHSB-2026-018) and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (AL26-29), along with an NVD record update. The vulnerability affects the optimized Base64 decoder used by HotSpot on modern Intel and AMD server CPUs. Servers commonly decode Base64 before authenticating users, including in HTTP Basic authentication headers, JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), SAML artifacts and file uploads. As a result, unauthenticated attackers may be able to reach the vulnerable code. Calif reports pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) against default configurations of several widely deployed Java products. Despite its name, Java4Shell differs significantly from Log4Shell. Exploitation requires specific CPU hardware, a just-in-time (JIT)-compiled decoder and an exploit chain tailored to each target. Exploitation is sensitive to timing and network conditions, with no universal payload or confirmed exploitation in the wild at the time of writing. Java4Shell warrants prompt, prioritized patching, but it is not another Log4Shell. We strongly recommend upgrading affected Java runtimes to the fixed builds listed below, prioritizing internet-facing identity providers and DevOps platforms.
